item.title: When Results Don’t Matter: What Fandom Teaches Brands About Loyalty
item.description: From relegation scraps to exploding phones, the strongest fandoms aren’t built on wins but on identity, belonging and a story people are proud to stay part of.

item.title: Why ‘Friction-Maxxing’ Is Catching On and Why Brands Are Starting to Care
item.description: From Polaroids to perfume stores with no websites, a cultural shift is pushing back against relentless convenience. As consumers add friction back into their lives, strategists and brands are exploring whether effort, not ease, could become the next marketing advantage.

item.title: From Worldbuilding To World Belonging: What Animal Crossing Can Teach Brand Experiences
item.description: A cozy island game where nothing much happens has quietly become a masterclass in building worlds people actually want to spend their time in. Here’s what brands can learn from games like Animal Crossing about designing calmer, more communal experiences offline.

item.title: Culture Isn’t a Channel: Jägermeister’s Kea Kleihauer on Earning Relevance
item.description: Brands can’t buy their way into culture. Jägermeister’s global head of culture and experiential, Kea Kleihauer, argues the case for usefulness and long‑term community investment over KPIs and quick wins.

item.title: Designing The Future We Actually Want
item.description: If we can’t picture the 22nd century, we can’t build it. Here’s how creative teams, brands and foresight thinkers can swap a commonly shared abstract and dystopian view of the future for something worth working toward.

item.title: Has The Word ‘Trend’ Lost Its Meaning?
item.description: Everyone’s chasing social “trends”, but the word has become shorthand for fads when it was meant for something deeper and more strategic. Industry insiders say it’s time to retire the term altogether, rethink the language we use and refocus on the underlying shifts that actually shape audiences.

item.description: Listen on Spotify Listen on Apple Music Watch on YouTube Welcome back to the Brandmakers podcast, where Hannah is joined by Ruth Henriquez who is head of licensing and partnerships at Mattel overseeing the IP for brands like Barbie, Hot Wheels, Uno and Masters of the Universe. item.title: Mattel’s IP Play: How The Toymaker Is Turning Into an Entertainment Powerhouse
item.description: Hannah Bowler dives into Mattel’s slow, deliberate shift from selling toys to building franchises – and asks its head of licensing and partnerships, Ruth Henriquez, about the decision of betting on fans, fast collabs and decades of nostalgia to make the model stick.

item.title: From Cost Centre to Growth Engine: How AI Has Pushed Creativity Center Stage
item.description: Thanks to AI we’re moving to one-to-one advertising. The catch is, it only works if you can produce and iterate enough distinct creative for the machines to find the right ad for the right person at the right moment. Creative is no longer a cost centre, it’s now the growth engine.

item.title: Sport as the Operating System for Culture
item.description: Sport has stopped being just a sponsorship channel and has slowly but surely become the operating system for culture. Leagues, brands and athletes can all win if they treat every fan touchpoint as part of an always‑on, integrated experience, rather than a row of logos on shirts or around a pitch.
